concept.name: Moving VWAP
concept.definition: A moving average of successive VWAP values over a user-chosen number of periods, producing a volume-weighted average that flows continuously from day to day instead of resetting each session.
concept.intuition: Classic VWAP dies at the close; MVWAP keeps a rolling volume-weighted memory, giving longer-horizon traders a VWAP-like reference across days.
concept.mechanics: Compute intraday VWAP as usual (cumulative typical price x volume over cumulative volume), then average the last n VWAP values; a 10-period MVWAP starts plotting after 10 VWAP points and slides forward, dropping the oldest.
concept.formula: MVWAP(n) = (1/n) x sum of the last n VWAP values, where each VWAP = sum(TypicalPrice x Volume) / sum(Volume) over its calculation window.
concept.failure_modes: Doubly smoothed, it lags more than plain VWAP, and its value depends on how each platform chains daily VWAPs across sessions; there is no single canonical construction.
concept.misconceptions: MVWAP has no end-of-day 'final value' significance the way daily VWAP does - it is a rolling average of averages, not an execution benchmark.
concept.example: If the last five daily VWAP values are 100, 101, 101.5, 102, 102.5, the 5-period MVWAP = 101.4.

citations.source: Trading With VWAP and MVWAP - Investopedia
